body: Investors are looking beyond AI to “real economy” stocks in the industrial, consumer defensive, and energy sectors. Industrial, consumer defensive, and energy stocks are outperforming the broader market by a wide margin, offsetting losses in technology, communication services, consumer cyclicals, and even financials. The industrials sector is responsible for 1.36 percentage points of the Morningstar US Market Index’s 0.93% gain this year through Feb. 18, according to Morningstar data. Caterpillar CAT and GE Vernova GEV have had the largest impact on the sector’s overall return. Consumer defensives are up 13.3% and account for a 0.6-point boost to the total market, with Walmart WMT and Costco Wholesale COST leading that sector. Energy stocks have seen even more dramatic gains and are up more than 22% since the start of the year. They have a smaller weighting in the US Market Index than industrials and consumer defensives, however, and account for a 0.64-point increase in the total market’s return.

Beyond the headlines, commentary and data flow, we find that the relative performance among major stock indexes from a perspective of sectors, market capitalizations and style can help keep things in perspective in times of turbulence and provide useful information as to what value the markets are attributing to the news and data flow from day to day. The same indices showed respective loses on a year -to -date basis as of the close last Friday of 5.17%, 4.95%, 6.86%, 0.27%, 0.7% and 1.75% as markets navigated turbulence generated from a number of things including heightened geopolitical risks, stickier than expected inflation along with expectations that the Fed is not likely to cut rates twice this year (as earlier expected by market participants) even as the economy has shown signs of slowing from mixed data on the consumer, business, jo b s and economic growth. As daunting as bears and skeptics may project the outcome of the current challenges to the market’s progress be, history suggests that opportunity might well indeed lie close to risk amidst the day -to -day volatility and churn reflected in the markets---even as the proverbial disclaimer reminds us that “past performance is no guarantee of future results”.
